items.title: Centre clears appointment of Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal as Chief Justice of Rajasthan High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal as the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court. The appointment comes pursuant to a recommendation made by the Supreme Court Collegium on August 31. Justice Agrawal is currently the Acting Chief Justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court. He was elevated as an additional judge of that Court in September 2013 and made a permanent judge in March 2016. His elevation as Chief Justice comes amid a controversy over the conduct of the present Acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma . Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta had recently written to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant seeking Justice Sharma's transfer out of Rajasthan and appointment of a regular Chief Justice from another High Court. Justice Mehta had raised allegations concerning Justice Sharma's exercise of administrative powers and the listing of cases. items.title: DVAC searches 30 places linked to KN Nehru, DMK chief Stalin alleges political vendetta
items.summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Saturday, September 5, conducted simultaneous searches at 30 locations in Chennai, Trichy, Coimbatore, Erode and Tiruppur in connection with alleged irregularities in tenders awarded by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department between 2021 and 2025, when former Minister KN Nehru held the portfolio. Properties linked to Nehru, his brothers and others were among those searched. The searches were based on an FIR registered by the DVAC Headquarters in Chennai against Nehru and 12 others over allegations including collection of party funds from tender awardees. The DVAC said it seized 241 documents and electronic evidence allegedly linked to irregularities in the tender process. According to a Times of India report, the searches were based on a communication sent by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the State government on December 3, 2025, alleging large-scale manipulation of MAWS tenders. The ED had alleged that at least Rs 1,020 crore was collected as bribes and commissions through manipulation of contracts. items.title: Centre clears appointment of Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi as Chief Justice of Bombay High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Allahabad High Court Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi as the new Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court. Justice Tripathi will be the 50th Chief Justice of the High Court and the second Chief Justice from Allahabad High Court. The recommendation for his appointment as the Chief Justice was made by the Supreme Court Collegium at a meeting held on August 6. Justice Tripathi graduated in law from Lucknow University in 1990. He enrolled as an advocate on January 11, 1992. His practice was mainly on the civil side. He served as the additional chief standing counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh since October 2007. He also appeared as counsel for the Kanpur Development Authority, Kanpur Nagar Nigam, UP Food and Essential Commodities Corporation, Agra Development Authority, Moradabad Development Authority and Kumaun University. Justice Tripathi was elevated as an additional judge of the Allahabad High Court on September 27, 2013. He was made a permanent judge on April 10, 2015. Bombay High Court is currently functioning with 74 judges as against its sanctioned strength of 94 judges.

items.title: Centre notifies appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as Chief Justice of Punjab & Haryana HC
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. Justice Mishra is currently serving as the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his elevation as the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court on August 6. Justice Mishra, who obtained his LL.B. from Delhi University's Campus Law Centre, was appointed as an additional judge of the Allahabad High Court on February 3, 2014, and was made a permanent judge on February 1, 2016. He served at the Allahabad High Court up to July 20, 2025 before being transferred to the Punjab and Haryana High Court, where he joined on July 21, 2025. He was appointed acting Chief Justice on June 1 following the elevation of then Chief Justice Sheel Nagu to the Supreme Court.

items.title: Justice RV Ghuge appointed Chief Justice of Calcutta High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Bombay High Court Justice Ravindra V Ghuge as the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his appointment on August 6. The same was cleared by the government on Saturday. Justice Ghuge is presently serving as the acting Chief Justice of Bombay High Court. A Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his elevation as the Chief Justice of Calcutta High Court on August 6. Justice Ghuge completed his law education from MP Law College in Aurangabad in 1990. He joined the Bar in 1990 and was elevated as the judge of the Bombay High Court in 2013. He was appointed as acting Chief Justice of the High Court after Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar was elevated to Supreme Court in June this year.

items.title: Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati appointed Chief Justice of J&K and Ladakh High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as the Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Justice Bhati is currently a judge of the Rajasthan High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his name for Chief Justice of J&K and Ladakh High Court on August 31. Justice Bhati will now take over as the Chief Justice from Justice Sanjeev Kumar who has been serving as acting Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since June 2. Justice Bhati was a lawyer practicing across several areas of law for nearly 25 years before he was elevated to the bench of the Rajasthan High Court on November 16, 2016. As a lawyer, he served as a Additional Advocate General for the State and was elected as President of the High Court Lawyers Association at different points Justice Bhati's wife, Justice Nupur Bhati, was also elevated as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

items.title: NLU Delhi confers Lifetime Achievement Award on Prof Upendra Baxi
items.summary: National Law University, Delhi (NLUD) on September 5, Teachers' Day, conferred the Lifetime Achievement Award on Prof (Dr) Upendra Baxi . Prof Baxi is a Distinguished Professor at NLU Delhi. He has also been a professor of law at Warwick University since 1996. He has also served as a Vice-Chancellor (VC) of Delhi University (DU) from 1990 to 1994, after over two decades as a professor there. He was earlier Vice Chancellor of the University of South Gujarat. In 2011, he was awarded the Padma Shri. The ceremony was held at the University Moot Court Hall, NLUd. NLU Delhi Vice Chancellor Prof (Dr) GS Bajpai delivered the welcome address. GALTER Founder Director Prof (Dr) MK Bhandari then spoke on the significance of the award. items.title: Centre does not want to collect even ₹1 in tax that is not due: ASG N Venkataraman
items.summary: Additional Solicitor General N Venkataraman has assured businesses that the Central government will support them in court if tax officials are found to have deliberately abused their authority. Venkataraman was speaking alongside Senior Advocate Arvind P Datar at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre (GHAC) Arbitration Week 2026 on September 5. The session at GIFT City Club was titled An Introduction to Investment Treaty Arbitration, BIT, Future of ISDS . The three-day event has been organised by the GHAC in collaboration with the Gujarat High Court. Advocates Uchit Sheth and Soham Patel facilitated the discussion. Venkataraman said the Centre did not want legitimate trade to suffer because of wrongful tax demands. “If you find somebody wrong, and they have deliberately used their authority to abuse, please bring it to the notice of the court, we will support you. It's a guarantee we give. We don't want to harm trade .” He added: “ We don't want to collect one rupee which is not due. Sure. We are mobilising the funds that are required.
